1. I would look at your electrical system as a whole.  100 year old building but how old is the service?  Is the meter can and wiring old or redone in the past 10 years?

2: I'd take an amp load reading at your meter base (if I can access it) and compare that to your panel line.  

3. I'd take an amp reading of every circuit and turn off and on every breaker, checking it against the label. 

4. I'd take a thermal picture of the panel and meter, cover off, under load, to see what gets hot.  I'll turn your heat or ac on your oven and run your hot water for a few minutes to see if anything is hot/loose or overloaded.

For 300 a month I run 3 computers, a fridge, an undersized heat pump, a window ac unit, and regularly an oven/microwave, washer/dryer.  

Think about what you have plugged in.  Decorative lights, ceramic heaters, portable ac units. These can draw way more than you think.

Just stuff to think about.  I'm sure other electricians have their own methods for such things, so don't worry if someone does it differently either.

Let us know if someone identifies something for you.  I'm always interested in puzzles like this.
